obligations.note: Commit 6d48175 changes required_approvals from `amount >= DUAL_CONTROL_THRESHOLD` to `amount > DUAL_CONTROL_THRESHOLD`, so a payment of exactly 10,000.00 now needs only one approver. PAY-1 requires two distinct approvers at or above the threshold, and the existing test_required_approvals_around_the_threshold asserts required_approvals(threshold) == 2.

Ticket CHG-25976 was approved by change manager erik.brandt on 2026-10-15, before the change opened on 2026-10-16. Its components (payments.payments, payments.tests) cover both touched paths per controls/payments/components.json.
The code_review approval is from mara.costa, a payments change_approver who is a different person from the author aisha.bello under all directory addresses.
The code_review approval names the head commit 6d48175, so it covers what would be merged.

The only CI run (records/ci/run.json) is on e6eb993. The later commit 6d48175 changes the dual-control comparison, which is a behaviour change, so the run does not count for the final commit. The PAY-1 control and unit tests would fail on head.

Ledger entry ACR-0401 (exhaustive PAY-1 proof) covers payments.py required_approvals, which this change alters in behaviour. That evidence has lapsed, and no new evidence of equal strength exists for the final commit.

The change deviates from PAY-1, but the exception register has no exception for PAY-1 or for payments.payments. The only entries are an expired SES-1 exception, a mortgage LOG-1 exception and a withdrawn MFA-1 exception.

summary: Besides adding the approvals_remaining helper, the change quietly replaces the dual-control comparison `>=` with `>`, so payments of exactly 10,000.00 would be released with a single approval. That violates PAY-1, and no exception covers it. CI evidence exists only for the earlier commit, and the later behaviour-changing commit voids it (CHG-4). It also lapses the prior PAY-1 proof (LAP-1). The ticket and code review approvals are in order, but the product-control violation alone requires rejection.
